commit_message:
Transitively dec-ref objects in the DRC collector (#10401)

* Transitively dec-ref objects in the DRC collector

Previously, the DRC collector only performed shallow reference counting where if
an object's ref count was decremented and reached zero, then we would deallocate
that object, but we would not decrement the reference counts of any other object
that was referenced by it. This commit changes that, so that now we will
decrement the reference counts of other objects referenced by an object that is
being deallocated.

This requires some method of tracing an object's outgoing edges. To avoid
needing to keep around and dispatch upon type-specific information about which
struct fields are GC references, for example, we instead pack all GC references
at the start of the object, just after its header. We additionally keep a count
of how many GC references an object has in its header. This allows us to create
a slice of any object's GC references, and we can uniformly trace any GC
object's outgoing edges. We don't need to reflect on the GC object's actual
type.

A final detail: the DRC collector was previously storing the object size in the
common GC header's reserved bits. It now stores the number of GC refs there
instead, and the object size is stored in its own field in the DRC-specific
header, next to the ref count. This is nice because, since we are making the DRC
header larger anyways, it raises the DRC collector's implementation limit on
object size from `u27::MAX` to `u32::MAX`.

Fixes #9701

* update disas tests

* Remove newly-added debug-assert that isn't true in certain edge cases

Sometimes we need to deallocate uninitialized objects when initializing their
fields fails, and this assertion trips.

* fix some tests by returning an error of the correct kind of trap

rather than a generic anyhow error

* fix tracing GC refs on big-endian architectures

We can't cast to a slice, we need to do conversion from little-endian bytes.

fix_commit.message: Fix a bug where arrays of GC refs were misreporting their count of GC edges (#10453)
fix_commit.author: Nick Fitzgerald

findings.title: GC array of GC-refs reports byte size instead of element count as num_gc_refs
findings.message: In `DrcCompiler::alloc_array` (crates/cranelift/src/gc/enabled/drc.rs), when allocating a `(array (ref ...))` whose elements are themselves GC references, the code computes `num_gc_refs` by reusing the `size` value returned from `emit_array_size`, which is the array's *total byte size* (base header size + len*elem_size), not the *count* of GC-reference elements. This `num_gc_refs` value is packed into the object's GC header (via `emit_gc_raw_alloc` -> `kind_and_reserved = kind | num_gc_refs`) and is later used by the DRC collector's tracing code to compute a slice of the object's outgoing GC-reference edges (count of `VMGcRef`-sized slots immediately following the header). Because `size` is numerically much larger than the true number of elements (and is a byte count rather than an element count), the collector believes the array has far more outgoing GC edges than it actually does. When tracing/dec-refing the array during collection, the GC walks past the end of the actual reference slots and off the end of the object/heap, reading and dec-refing arbitrary heap memory as if it were `VMGcRef` values. This is a heap buffer over-read (and consequent corruption of unrelated heap data via spurious ref-count decrements/frees) triggered simply by creating and then collecting a guest array-of-GC-refs value.
findings.suggestion: Use the array's element length (not its total byte size) when computing `num_gc_refs` for arrays whose elements are GC references. Refactor `emit_array_size` to take the already-computed `len` value instead of the `ArrayInit` (so the length can be reused), compute `len` once via `init.len(...)`, pass it into `emit_array_size`, and set `num_gc_refs = len` (the element count) instead of `num_gc_refs = size` (the byte size) when `array_layout.elems_are_gc_refs` is true.

ground_truth.root_cause: The commit that introduced transitive dec-ref tracing in the DRC collector (#10401) added a new `num_gc_refs` header field used to bound the slice of outgoing GC edges traced during collection. For arrays of GC-ref elements, the author intended to pass the array length but accidentally reused the `size` local (the array's byte size in memory, computed by `emit_array_size`), since both were available in scope and the mistake (size vs. len) was an easy one given they are used adjacently. There was no type-level distinction between a 'byte size' ir::Value and an 'element count' ir::Value, so the compiler could not catch the mismatch.
